editorial:
Have you ever wondered who would actually show up to your funeral if you died tomorrow? That is exactly what Michael is thinking. He is a total nightmare of a person who works as a meter maid and spends every second of his day obsessed with social media. He is loud, annoying, and pretty much hated by everyone he knows. To satisfy his curiosity, he comes up with a wild plan to fake his own death just to see which of his so-called friends actually care enough to attend the service. It is a funny, cringey setup that feels like a social experiment gone wrong.

The acting is great because it makes you love to hate the main character. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is worth it. If you like dark humor and seeing an arrogant person get their comeuppance, you will enjoy this. It is a light watch that does not take itself too seriously. You can grab it as a rental on Apple TV or stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a solid move.
endingExplained: In the end, Michael realizes that most of the people he thought were his friends are actually fake. The big twist comes when he sees who truly cared for him versus who was just pretending for the cameras. After the chaos of the funeral settles, Michael is forced to face the truth about his own behavior. He ends up learning a hard lesson about friendship and humility, finally understanding that being liked online means nothing in the real world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about people getting a taste of their own medicine.
